dialect.detail: NIST CCVS (Cobol Compiler Validation System) test suite, version 4.2 April 1993. Uses XXXXX placeholder tokens for implementor-specific names (SOURCE-COMPUTER, OBJECT-COMPUTER, file assignments). Tests relative I-O file processing.

purpose.domain_detail: NIST CCVS COBOL-85 conformance validation suite — relative I-O sequential access testing
purpose.summary: This is the third program in a series of NIST CCVS tests for relative file I-O. It reads a relative file created by RL109A sequentially, verifies all 500 records for accuracy, selectively deletes records, and then re-verifies the remaining records. It is part of the official COBOL 85 compiler validation system.

notable_features: ORGANIZATION IS RELATIVE with SEQUENTIAL access mode
VALUE OF implementor-name clauses (C/G conditional lines)
XXXXX placeholder tokens for portability across implementations
REDEFINES for numeric picture variants (COMPUTED-A, CORRECT-A)
No EXEC SQL, no EXEC CICS, no COMP-3
High PERFORM count (61) and GOTO count (24) typical of CCVS harness
verdict.notes: File is truncated to first 16000 chars out of 50381 bytes (622 lines total). The CCVS framework is well-known; classification is high confidence. The 'C' and 'G' indicator lines in columns 7 are CCVS conditional compilation markers for VALUE OF clauses. No vendor-specific dialect features visible; designed to be portable across COBOL-85 compilers.
